purpose: The preceding paragraph defines stiffness degradation and its simplifying assumption. This paragraph explains why a short-window linear approximation permits online stability analysis, while preserving its limits. The next paragraph can then apply the degradation factor in the virtual RTHS study.
first_draft: Because structural degradation is nonlinear and time varying, the analysis uses a short-window linear approximation for tractable online evaluation. The approximation may not be accurate during brief intervals when properties change rapidly, but it is typically accurate before and after those events and when degradation evolves slowly.
review: The draft covers the nonlinear and time-varying behavior, the reason for the approximation, and both accuracy qualifications. Its second sentence combines the limitation and the typical-accuracy conditions, so I split them to make the qualification easier to follow. The final sentences contain 1, 0, and 0 prose commas. The first sentence follows the preceding stiffness-degradation model; the last prepares the gradual-degradation analysis that follows.
final: Structural degradation is nonlinear and time varying, so the analysis uses a short-window linear approximation to remain tractable and suitable for online evaluation. This approximation may not be accurate during brief intervals when structural properties change rapidly. It is typically accurate before and after these intervals and while degradation evolves slowly.
